narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the increasing proportion of voters residing in landslide counties from 1976 to 2016.

units.meaning: The clip must identify the three election years in the data series: 1976, 2012, and 2016.
accepted_routes: Names 1976, 2012, and 2016 as the series years
Shows the three years in chronological order
Identifies the three data points by election year
units.visual_evidence_rule: The labels 1976, 2012, and 2016 must be legible and associated with the three data points.
units.reviewer_question: Must all three years be named, or are the endpoints sufficient?

units.meaning: The relative value is higher in each later year than in the previous year, establishing an increasing trend/order: 1976 < 2012 < 2016.

basis.note: lowest value in the ordered series
middle value in the ordered series
highest value in the ordered series

accepted_routes: The relative share rises in each successive year
Later years have higher relative values than earlier years
1976 is lowest, 2012 is middle, 2016 is highest
The proportion increases from 1976 to 2012 to 2016
units.visual_evidence_rule: A viewer must be able to compare the three relative values and see the monotonic increase.
units.temporal_anchor: The overall increase narrative across the 1976, 2012, and 2016 clauses.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly convey monotonic increase across all three years?

units.meaning: The starting endpoint in 1976 has relative value 0.2787.
accepted_routes: 1976 begins at a relative value of 0.2787
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1976 data point's relative value must be visible or readable as 0.2787.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 1976 starting relative value required as a specific starting endpoint?

units.meaning: The ending endpoint in 2016 has relative value 0.5972.
accepted_routes: 2016 ends at a relative value of 0.5972
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2016 data point's relative value must be visible or readable as 0.5972.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 2016 ending relative value required as a specific ending endpoint?

units.meaning: The total 1976-to-2016 increase is 0.3185 in relative value, and the 2016 relative value is about 2.14 times the 1976 relative value.
accepted_routes: The relative value increases by 0.3185 from 1976 to 2016
2016 relative value is about 2.14 times the 1976 relative value
The 1976-to-2016 rise is 0.5972 minus 0.2787 = 0.3185 relative units
The endpoint relative share is more than double the starting relative share
units.visual_evidence_rule: The visual must allow seeing the magnitude of the 1976-to-2016 increase, not just its direction.
units.temporal_anchor: The overall clause describing change from 1976 to 2016.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the total 1976-to-2016 increase, or is direction alone enough?

optional_valid: The 2012 relative_value 0.4976 lies between the 1976 and 2016 values.
The 2012 relative_value 0.4976 is closer to the 2016 value than to the 1976 value: differences are 0.0996 versus 0.2189.
The 2012 relative_value 0.4976 is above the midpoint of the 1976 and 2016 endpoints: midpoint 0.43795.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any absolute percentage, count, or dollar value, including the narration's 28%, 50%, and 60%.
Causal explanations for why voters moved or why landslide counties changed.
Claims about party, geography, polarization, or other topics not present in the table.
Layout or rendering claims about bar positions, colors, axis ticks, or chart type.
notes: All numeric content is relative-only; decimals are table relative_value, not percentages. The units separate three-year identity, monotonic ordering, endpoints, and derived total change so reviewers can decide what is mandatory.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
